Resolves #19478

A first-mount resolver can queue another update and then throw before common VDOM settlement. The initial failure now rejects its parked requests, releases its captured waiters and lets dirty rendering recover. Cleanup checks the component and initialization attempt, so an older failure cannot retire a newer initialization or a reused-ID replacement.

Evidence: L2 (real Component/Helper failure sequences) with L3 Workstation success controls → L2 required (failure-liveness and ownership ACs). No residuals.

Change class: restoration. agent-preflight: not hosted here; normal Engine pre-commit checks passed and the shared baseline jobs run on this PR.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | New `VdomLifecycle.spec.mjs` mount-resolver arm fails before repair with a permanently pending late request; the repair rejects it with the original failure. |
| AC-2 | The same arm observes the queued class rendered and the flight/callback state cleared. |
| AC-3 | Controls cover reentrant rejection, new phase work, a reused-ID replacement, overlapping same-instance initialization and captured waiters when rejection starts a retry. |
| AC-4 | Existing `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` first-render/unmounted-child controls pass unchanged; `WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs` preserves the browser await-mount consumers. |
| AC-5 | Error reproduction is explicitly unit-runtime evidence; the browser controls test successful boot/recovery, not an observed application outage. |

## Deltas from ticket

An overlapping-initialization falsifier required a private per-initialization token, removed when its attempt ends. It is confined to initialization; the ordinary update/settlement path is unchanged. Existing manager rejection and captured post-update primitives own callback handling. The accepted not-yet-mounted success exception from #18802 remains.

## Test Evidence

[Validation receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19478#issuecomment-6074894570) records the red controls and final results. The two original failure probes fail before repair. Additional overlap and waiter controls caught intermediate ownership mistakes and pass after correction.

`npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/workstation/WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs`: 6/6 browser controls passed. The final focused pair passed 38 tests; the full unit suite passed 4,871 with 2 skipped. Expected injected-error logs do not represent failing tests.

## Comments

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-10-09T06:09:38Z

Follow-up to Ada's non-blocking hypothesis in [review 5466323491](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19483#pullrequestreview-5466323491), tested on unchanged `ba1b4ef343`.

A real Component/VDomUpdate/Helper control holds the current `Helper.create` call **before any vnode is created**, changes the class to `dirty-before-mount`, queues `promiseUpdate`, then rejects the create call with one sentinel error. No newer initialization exists at rejection time.

Observed after cleanup:
- Initial attempt and parked request both reject with that original error.
- `mounted=false`, `isVnodeInitializing=false`, `isVdomUpdating=false`; flight and promise-callback registries are empty.
- `needsVdomUpdate=true`: unmounted dirty work remains explicitly retryable.

Restoring the real creator, queuing another `promiseUpdate`, and calling `initVnode(true)` fulfills both new promises; the component mounts with `dirty-before-mount`, clears the dirty flag and leaves no in-flight entry. All assertions pass. The control uses the existing single-thread unit wiring and a no-op Main delta sink; it is L2 evidence, not an installed/browser failure receipt.

This falsifies the proposed liveness concern for that arm. No tracked source or tests changed, and the approved head remains unchanged.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19478, starting with its Design authority line: the `promiseUpdate` failure contract must not strand parked requests, and the not-yet-mounted success exception stays binding. Then its Contract Ledger and ACs; `initVnode` and the merged #19479 settlement API (`rejectPromiseCallbacks`, `triggerPostUpdates(id, snapshot)`); and the #18802 NOT_PLANNED ruling, under which the render that mounts a component settles every request parked on it.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** On failure, `initVnode` rejects the requests parked under its own flight with the original error and keeps dirty work retryable. It touches the registry, flags and waiters only while this component and this attempt still own them, so an old failure can't retire a newer same-instance attempt or a reused-ID replacement. No change to the success path or to ordinary settlement, and no global tracker. Tests are real Component/Helper unit sequences; the failure arms need no browser.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. The catch acts only when `Neo.getComponent(id) === me` and the per-attempt Symbol still names this attempt. It detaches its post-update queue before any callback runs, clears the flags, unregisters the flight and only then rejects. Waiters run from the detached snapshot, and the dirty retry is guarded by `!me.isVdomUpdating`. The `finally` removes the token only while it is still this attempt's.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. AC-5 keeps the injected-exception unit evidence distinct from any observed browser symptom, and the success contract is preserved rather than re-argued.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: The cleanup ownership you flagged holds. Here is the ordering I traced. When a rejection callback starts a newer initialization, the newer attempt's synchronous part runs before the old cleanup continues: it sets a new token, re-registers the flight and raises `isVdomUpdating` again. The old cleanup then releases its snapshot's waiters, which yield to the newer flight. Its `me.update()` is skipped by the `!me.isVdomUpdating` guard, and its `finally` leaves the newer token alone. One arm is not pinned by a test: the **current** attempt failing **before** mount (for example `Helper.create` rejecting with no newer attempt) while dirty work is queued. The overlap test covers a pre-mount failure only for a superseded attempt, and the mount-resolver test covers only a failure after `mounted` is set. I didn't trace what the guarded `me.update()` does on a still-unmounted component in that arm. The `promiseUpdate` contract (the mounting render settles parked work) suggests a later mount picks the work up, which would satisfy AC-2's "remains explicitly retryable". Non-blocking; *hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation* if anyone wants the pin.
